label: late-episode clock: unrewarded D1 and a1 GO steps in the last ~15 trials
explanation: The low end of candidate unit 36 tracks how far into the episode the agent is. It never fires in trials 0-9, almost never before trial 50, and 75% of its activation mass falls in trials 90-99, where it is active on 32% of steps. It also tracks the value head: 77% of mass is in the lowest value bin (value < 5.22), i.e. the agent anticipates that the episode is ending. It fires only at D1 and GO (63% / 37% of mass), never at D2 when a state is input. At D1 it is suppressed by a reward input (in_rew = 1 holds 1.4% of mass). At GO it prefers trials where the agent is about to choose a1 (policy logit favouring a1). Activation within a window grows trial by trial toward the episode end (rel +1 D1 is the largest cell), and the top examples are long runs of unrewarded D1s late in the episode. Predicate: late episode (ep_trial >= 85) AND (an unrewarded D1 OR a GO where the agent chooses a1). action at GO is the agent's own upcoming choice, which is legitimate, so this uses no future random outcome. Dev scores: P 0.73, R 0.57, F1 0.64, mass recall 0.76. Late episode + not D2 alone gives F1 0.50 / mass recall 0.85; value < 5.22 does about as well as the ep_trial cut. Misses are weak activations at D1 before trial 85, or unrewarded D1s in a1-preferring contexts. False positives are mostly a2 GO steps and quiet late steps. It acts like a graded episode-clock / low-value signal more than a binary event detector.
